messages:
Alex (Support): Hi team — customer on Private is failing to upload the collected archive. They say the collector completes, but upload errors out with a 403. Need repro steps and what to ask the customer for.
Jasmine (Customer): The agent finished: `collector v2.1.3` on our VM, then we see `upload failed: 403` in stdout. Request id in logs: `req=cs-8b7c2e`. We ran with --redact=auto. Host is behind corp proxy and strict outbound rules.
Alex (Support): Thanks. Can you paste the full collector stdout lines around the upload attempt (3-5 lines)? Also we need the `redaction_summary.json` from the bundle root and the collector config (sanitized). If you can run a reproduction curl against the presign URL, that helps.
Jasmine (Customer): Pasting minimal excerpt:
```
2026-12-18T09:12:02Z collector starting upload to https://artifacts.internal.example.com/presign/abc123
2026-12-18T09:12:03Z upload failed status=403 body="Access Denied" req=cs-8b7c2e
2026-12-18T09:12:03Z retrying (1/3)
```
Jasmine (Customer): redaction_summary.json attached in bundle (shows 0 PII redacted) — suspicious since there should be IPs.
Tom (Eng): Two quick asks: 1) full collector cmdline + config file (or `cat /etc/collector/config.yml | sed -e 's/password:.*/password: <redacted>/'`) 2) `curl -v` reproduction against the presigned PUT URL. Example curl we want them to run:
```
curl -v -X PUT "https://artifacts.internal.example.com/presign/abc123" -H "Content-Type: application/gzip" --data-binary @bundle-20261218.tar.gz
```
Tom (Eng): Also note: if their outbound proxy rewrites signatures or strips Authorization header, S3 style presigns will 403. Ask if there's any transparent proxy or WAF.
Mia (SRE): Add ask for `iptables -L -n` and `getenforce` (SELinux state) and any HTTP(S) proxy env vars in the service environment (`HTTP_PROXY`, `HTTPS_PROXY`, `NO_PROXY`). If SELinux is enforcing, maybe collector couldn't open temp socket for chunked upload.
Jasmine (Customer): I ran the curl from the VM and got:
```
*   Trying 10.1.2.3:443...
* Connected to artifacts.internal.example.com (10.1.2.3) port 443 (#0)
> PUT /presign/abc123 HTTP/1.1
> Host: artifacts.internal.example.com
> User-Agent: curl/7.68.0
> Accept: */*
> Content-Type: application/gzip
> Content-Length: 123456
> 
< HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden
< Date: Fri, 18 Dec 2026 09:12:03 GMT
< Content-Type: application/xml
< x-amz-request-id: TXN9X7QZ
< x-amz-error-code: AccessDenied
< Content-Length: 123
< 
* Connection #0 to host artifacts.internal.example.com left intact
```
Alex (Support): Good reproduction. Next: ask them to capture `tcpdump -w upload.pcap host artifacts.internal.example.com and port 443` while running the curl — to see if a proxy is mutating headers. Also request the collector bundle's `manifests/metadata.json` and the file `redaction_summary.json` content pasted.
Jasmine (Customer): I can get tcpdump capture but it's sensitive — we'll send via SFTP to your secure upload host. The machine restricts outbound to only certain IPs, S3 stores are internal. We can scp to support-only jumpbox.
Mia (SRE): Ok — alternate upload path: have them run the collector again with `--archive-path /tmp/bundle.tar.gz --no-upload` to generate local artifact, then scp to support jumpbox. Example:
```
collector collect --config /etc/collector/config.yml --archive-path /tmp/bundle-$(date +%s).tar.gz --no-upload
scp /tmp/bundle-*.tar.gz support-jumpbox:/incoming/jasmine
```
Tom (Eng): If they can't scp, ask for the minimal logs showing the presign URL generation on the control plane side (we need the presign token / expiry & service principal id) — we'll check the signature on our side. Also confirm collector version (you said v2.1.3) and whether `--redact=auto` might have failed; ask them to re-run with `--redact=full` to force redaction and compare `redaction_summary.json`.
Jasmine (Customer): Will try scp to jumpbox later today. In the meantime I found an extra header in our proxy that strips Authorization for requests over 5MB — we think it's opaque to us. Could this cause 403 only for bigger bundles? The curl worked for a tiny test file (1KB) but 403 for the real bundle.
Tom (Eng): Yes that matches a proxy behavior: small requests pass through, chunked/large uploads go via different policy and have Auth trimmed. That will 403 because presigned URL includes signature in query string and backend expects full/unaltered request. Workaround: upload in smaller chunks or use the scp fallback. Long term: we'll add a helper that pushes via control-plane proxy for Private deployments.
Alex (Support): For now, ask them to: 1) run `collector collect --no-upload` and scp the archive to us; 2) paste `redaction_summary.json` and `manifests/metadata.json`; 3) run the curl -v output and tcpdump if they can. We'll open a secure S3 object for temporary upload if jumpbox not possible.
automation-bot: Created support ticket INC-20261218-4289 and pre-provisioned temporary SFTP: sftp://support-jumpbox/incoming/jasmine (expires in 24h).
Jasmine (Customer): Thanks, starting collect now and will scp when done. ETA 45m.
Tom (Eng): Once we have bundle, we'll validate presign signature via the x-amz-request-id and our control plane logs, and also check redaction tool behavior on their host. If proxy is the cause, short-term workaround is `--no-upload` + scp or run collector inside a bastion with no proxy.
Alex (Support): Great — I'll follow up in this thread after we get the bundle. :thumbsup:
